title: Show HN: Dualayer Hierarchy Standard (DHS) – Zero-FHS Layout for Musl and Glibc
description: Dualayer Hierarchy Standard (DHS: Repo: https://github.com/Zainium-Dynamics/dualayer-hierarchy-stand... Full Specification (23-page PDF): https://zainiumdynamics.tech/dhs DHS 1.1 defines a layered filesystem hierarchy for immutable Linux systems where musl and glibc coexist side by side without conflict. Either C library can be primary; the distribution chooses. Root layout (no /usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib, /lib64, /etc, /var, or /boot at /, not even as symlinks): / |-- overlayer/ (the entire OS: all layers) |-- home/ (user home directories) |-- root/ (root home) |-- dev/ (devtmpfs) |-- proc/ (procfs) |-- sys/ (sysfs) |-- run/ (tmpfs; removable media at /run/media/user/label) `-- tmp/ (temporary files) Layer structure under /overlayer (composed at boot via OverlayFS with syshub as lower and userland/union as upper): /overlayer/ |-- syshub/ (read-only base OS; boots without userland) |-- userland/ (installed packages: union/, work/, registry/) |-- ignition/ (kernels, initramfs, bootloader; read-o
